source_refs.note: Weightlessness in Satellites: a main subheading of 3.3 Artificial satellites, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 62-62.

blocks.text: When a satellite is launched by a rocket in its desired orbit around the Earth, then it has been observed practically that everything inside the satellite experiences weightlessness because the satellite is accelerating towards the centre of the Earth as a freely falling body.
Your weight slightly changes when the velocity of the elevator changes at the start and end of a ride, not during the rest of the ride when that velocity is constant.
blocks.title: Do You Know?

blocks.text: Consider a satellite of mass M revolving in its orbit of radius r around the Earth. A body of mass m inside the satellite suspended by a spring balance from the ceiling of the satellite is under the action of two forces. That is, its weight mg acting downward, while the supporting force, called normal force F_N or tension in the spring acting upward, as shown in Fig. 3.13. Their resultant force is equal to the centripetal force required by the mass m which is acting towards the centre of the Earth, and is expressed as:

blocks.alt: The Earth with its centre marked, inside a dotted circular orbit of radius r. At the top of the orbit a box, the satellite, holds a spring balance with a hanging mass. Arrows on the box: F_N upward, F_g = GmM/r² downward towards the Earth, and an orange arrow v along the orbit. Beside it, a free-body sketch of the hanging mass shows F_N = 0 N upward and F_g = GmM/r² downward.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.13: A mass on a spring balance inside a satellite orbiting the Earth (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.13).

blocks.text: When a bucket full of water is rapidly whirled in a vertical circular path, water does not fall out even if the bucket is inverted at the maximum height. Why is it so?
blocks.title: Can you tell?

blocks.text: It may be noted that the centripetal force responsible for the revolution of the satellite around the Earth is provided by the gravitational force of attraction between the Earth and the satellite.

This shows that the supporting force which is acting on a body inside the satellite is zero. Therefore, the bodies as well as the astronauts in a satellite find themselves in a state of apparent weightlessness.
